A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCTD study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite added sections and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of MCTD and baselines on maze navigation, cube manipulation, and visual planning, including success rates, runtime measurements, and appendix experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds component ablations and sensitivity experiments in Section 5.6 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The core tree rollout, guidance meta-actions, jumpy denoising, architecture, training objective, and Algorithms 1–10 remain substantively unchanged. Appendix A.6.7 newly documents cube-release and arm-positioning operations in the existing manipulation setup without establishing that the procedure changed between versions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate pointmaze and antmaze navigation, one-to-four-cube manipulation, visual pointmaze, and short-horizon stitch datasets. The new ablations reuse PointMaze navigate tasks without adding datasets, task requirements, or input-environment conditions.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets, including the appendix goal-inpainting variants, are retained. V3 adds component-focused controls: a greedy tree-search baseline in Table 4 and Diffusion Forcing and MCTD variants without causal denoising in Table 7.

E3.justification: V3 substantially expands the controlled evaluation design: greedy branching widths of 5–20, five guidance sets, subplan counts of 1/3/5/20, causal-denoising and tree-search controls, UCT weights from 0 to 10, and jumpiness settings including one-shot decoding. These are new experimental protocols; previously stated benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2's compute-scaling, stitching, goal-inpainting, and visual-failure analyses are retained. Section 5.6 and Appendix D add systematic tests of greedy search, guidance-set sensitivity, subplan length, causal denoising and tree search, UCT weighting, and simulation jumpiness, directly examining MCTD's central design choices.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five tasks per environment, ten seeds per model/task, and mean ± standard deviation reporting in Appendix A.4. V3's A.5.7 newly discloses three AntMaze trials per task/seed with the best outcome retained. This adds run-count and aggregation information without establishing an increase in trials.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark results remain unchanged, including Tables 1–3, Figure 6, and v2 Tables 8–9 becoming v3 Tables 12–13. New ablation results are substantial: Table 7 reports giant-maze success of 18 ± 11% without causal denoising versus 100 ± 0% for MCTD; Table 15 reports 10 ± 21% for one-shot simulation versus 100 ± 0% at C=10. These are new comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The existing equations and mathematical reasoning are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or formal assumption. Appendix D.1 explicitly states the standard UCT formula for the already-used selection criterion to explain its parameter sweep.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: integrating the four MCTS stages with diffusion planning through tree rollout, guidance meta-actions, and fast simulation, with improved planning and compute scalability. Replacing TTC terminology with inference-time wording does not change their meaning.

C2.justification: The added analyses substantially expand interpretation: diverse guidance options matter more than precise scales, excessive tree depth can exhaust search budgets, greedy search suffers from limited backtracking, and aggressive denoising jumps impair value estimation on harder tasks. These mechanism explanations and speed–accuracy qualifications are new; Section 6's existing limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: V3 adds specific reproducibility details, including the default UCT weight of 1.141, five-child branching, one-shot decoding from fully denoised predictions, and automatic cube release and arm pre-positioning in Appendix A.6.7. Existing architecture and training hyperparameter tables and repository access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds Jurgenson et al. (2020) on subgoal trees and de Waard et al. (2016) on high-level MCTS to acknowledge earlier planning approaches. Most other reference changes update existing works' publication information, including Anonymous becoming Ye et al. for the chess diffusion paper.

P1.justification: Existing prose and narrative organization are largely retained. V3 revises TTC/test-time terminology, expands DDIM, updates publication and reference text, and adds cross-references. It inserts Section 5.6 and an additional-results Appendix D, moving the existing algorithms appendix to E without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the experimental displays with four main-text ablation tables and two appendix tables covering success, runtime, and search counts. Figures 1–7 are retained, existing appendix tables are renumbered and relocated, and algorithm comments are realigned with changed spacing.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses an important gap in v2 by directly testing MCTD's central components and quantifying sensitivity and computational tradeoffs in Section 5.6 and Appendix D. Execution and trial-selection disclosures also improve transparency. Unexplained Diffusion Forcing score differences between Tables 1 and 7 limit cross-experiment interpretation, but the added component evidence substantially strengthens the paper's empirical justification.
